what: Hand adjudication of every disagreement sampled by heldout_conditional.detector_audit between the committed token-based detector and a naive raw-text one. 32 cases, 8 per predicate, seed 20260905.
result: 32/32 resolved in favour of the token detector. Every disagreement is a string literal or a comment: the naive detector cannot see the difference, the token one can. Note the direction — 6 of the 8 'expressed' disagreements are naive FALSE / token TRUE, i.e. the token detector is the more SENSITIVE of the two, which is the direction that matters for the zero cells.
bound: The disagreement rate (1.16% / 0.37% / 1.79% / 0.38% of 87,730 drafts) bounds the difference between two independent implementations, not the joint error. Cases where BOTH are wrong are not priced by this comparison; the raw-text robustness check below is what covers the headline zeros.

raw_text_robustness_of_the_zero_cells.uppercase_boolean: Of the 1,996 first-applicable (always untaught) drafts, 13 contain AND/OR/NOT anywhere in the raw text including strings and comments, and 0 use one as an operator. All 13 were read: 10 are comments, 3 are string literals or domain tokens (two of them are problems ABOUT boolean operators, where the model writes `if op == 'AND': res = res and array[i]` — the string is uppercase, the operator is not). So the 0/1,996 survives even a maximally permissive detector.
raw_text_robustness_of_the_zero_cells.grouped_large_integer: Of the 1,633 first-applicable drafts whose prompt showed no grouped literal, 0 contain a grouped literal anywhere in the raw text. No detector question arises.

teaching_detector: Exact substring of a machine-generated interpreter message, matched only against tool output. 0 of 87,730 drafts contain either teaching message in their own code, so the model cannot manufacture a match.
